title: The 'Star That Disappeared'—A Beacon That Just Went Dark
hook: A star in a nearby galaxy vanished from telescopes overnight, with no debris, no supernova—as if it was switched off.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea of a star being erased from existence taps into deep fears of cosmic impermanence and unknown forces.

title: The 'Signal That Came From Inside the Moon'—An Artificial Pulse
hook: A radio pulse was detected coming from the lunar subsurface—and it matched no known natural or human source.
why_this_can_go_viral: The moon being 'alive' or inhabited is a classic conspiracy hook, now backed by real data.

title: The 'Extinction Asteroid That Came From Nowhere'—No Orbit Found
hook: An asteroid the size of a mountain appeared on a collision course with Earth—and its trajectory suggests it was never part of our solar system.
why_this_can_go_viral: The fear of a 'stealth' asteroid that can't be tracked plays on existential vulnerability.

title: The 'Classified NASA Asteroid Redirect'—A Secret 1998 Mission
hook: Declassified documents suggest NASA attempted to nudge a near-Earth asteroid in 1998—but the mission was scrubbed and buried.
why_this_can_go_viral: Conspiracy enthusiasts love 'suppressed' missions—especially ones involving planetary defense.

title: The 'Fermi Paradox Tombstone'—A Signal That Says 'We Were Here'
hook: A repeating signal from a dead star system contains a simple binary message: coordinates of their homeworld—and the date of their extinction.
why_this_can_go_viral: A 'last message' from an alien civilization is emotionally devastating and highly shareable.

title: The 'Star That Ate Its Own Planet'—A Meal Caught on Camera
hook: For the first time, astronomers watched a star swallow a Jupiter-sized planet whole—and it sent a shockwave through the system.
why_this_can_go_viral: The visceral imagery of a star eating a planet is both fascinating and terrifying.

title: The 'Signal That Was a Map'—An Alien Star Chart Found in Radio Noise
hook: A anomalous signal from Proxima Centauri wasn't random—it encoded a map of a neighboring star system with an unknown world.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea of receiving an alien map taps into discovery and potential threat.

title: The 'Rogue Planet That Carries an Ocean of Acid'—A Floating Hell
hook: A planet with no star drifts through interstellar space, its surface a global ocean of sulfuric acid—and it's heading toward the Oort Cloud.
why_this_can_go_viral: A wandering death-world approaching our system is pure cosmic horror.

title: The 'Classified Soviet Space Weapon That Targeted Stars'
hook: In the 1980s, the USSR developed a laser weapon designed to dazzle enemy satellites—but declassified files reveal it was tested on a star.
why_this_can_go_viral: Cold War secrecy plus a target in deep space creates a compelling mystery.

title: The 'Extinction Event That Came From the Sun's Twin'—A Hidden Nemesis
hook: A long-theorized binary companion to the Sun, Nemesis, may have sent a comet swarm that caused a mass extinction—and it's coming back.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea of a hidden death star with a periodic cycle is a classic viral hook.

title: The 'Dark Matter Signal That Came From the Earth's Core'
hook: Scientists detected a dark matter signal deep underground—suggesting our planet is being bombarded by invisible particles from its own center.
why_this_can_go_viral: The Earth's core as an unknown frontier always sparks curiosity.

title: The 'Fermi Paradox Guardian'—A Signal That Blocks Communication
hook: Every time we transmit into deep space, a 'jamming' signal from an unknown origin scrambles the message—we're being silenced.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea of an external force actively preventing our cosmic communication is both paranoid and thrilling.

title: The 'Asteroid That Sheared a Mountain'—A Near Miss in 2019
hook: An asteroid passed so close to Earth in 2019 that its gravity tore a 200-meter chunk off a mountain in the Andes—no one noticed.
why_this_can_go_viral: A real, unnoticed event that shows how close we are to disaster is inherently viral.

title: The 'Pulsar That Beats Like a Human Heart'—A Cosmic Rhythm
hook: A pulsar 1,000 light-years away pulses at exactly 1.2 Hz—the resting heart rate of a human—and it's been doing so for eons.
why_this_can_go_viral: The uncanny connection between a star and the human body triggers awe and wonder.

title: The 'Classified Apollo 20 Mission'—A Ship Found on the Moon
hook: Leaked audio from a purported Apollo 20 mission describes an alien spacecraft found on the far side of the Moon—NASA denies everything.
why_this_can_go_viral: The most famous 'leaked' space conspiracy—it's evergreen and incredibly shareable.

title: The 'Signal That Was a Warning'—A Message From a Dead Alien
hook: A decoded message from a distant star system read: 'Do not follow this beacon. They will find you.'
why_this_can_go_viral: A direct warning from space is the ultimate clickbait—it's terrifying and mysterious.

title: The 'Extinction Comet That Split in Two'—Double Death Heading Our Way
hook: A massive comet from the Oort Cloud fractured into two equal pieces—both on a trajectory that will intersect Earth's orbit in 2078.
why_this_can_go_viral: A clear, imminent date with a double threat is pure viral fuel.

title: The 'Fermi Paradox Doomsday'—Civilizations Die Within 500 Years
hook: Statistical analysis of exoplanet data suggests any technological civilization destroys itself within 500 years of inventing radio.
why_this_can_go_viral: It directly applies to humanity—a terrifying statistical death sentence.

title: The 'Rogue Star That Tore a Planet From Its Orbit'—A Cosmic Theft
hook: A rogue star passed through a planetary system and yanked a gas giant away—now that planet wanders alone, stolen.
why_this_can_go_viral: The personification of a star as a 'thief' is a simple, compelling story.

title: The 'Classified X-37B Payload'—A Secret Space Plane's Unknown Mission
hook: The US Air Force's X-37B space plane has spent over 900 days in orbit—and a leaked document hints it's carrying a weapon that targets asteroids.
why_this_can_go_viral: The secrecy around the X-37B is a perfect conspiracy magnet.

title: The 'Extinction Solar Flare That Hits Every 1,000 Years'—We're Overdue
hook: Evidence from tree rings shows a solar flare powerful enough to destroy electronics hits Earth roughly every millennium—the last one was in 774 AD.
why_this_can_go_viral: A concrete, repeating threat with a clear historical precedent is terrifyingly relatable.
